reason: E3 directly supports the core premises that nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn at GBs reduces cohesion and causes ductility loss, and that shifting segregation to secondary phases avoids this. However, the hypothesis adds a specific mechanism (sluggish diffusion) not mentioned in the cited evidence, and E1 and E2 are irrelevant to the key premises (E1 discusses oxidation/precipitation in a different alloy, E2 describes ductile fracture in a multi-phase wire).
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces grain boundary cohesion in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi.
This nanosegregation promotes intergranular cracking and ductility loss.
Sluggish diffusion in HEAs mediates the elemental distribution at grain boundaries.
Shifting segregation into pre-existing secondary phases can avoid ductility loss.
